groups.title: CreateBucket on a bucket the caller already owns returns 409
groups.why: fakes3 answers 409 `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou`. AWS (us-east-1, the only region fakes3 pretends to be) answers 200 and keeps the bucket (legacy behaviour documented under CreateBucket errors). `test_bucket_create_exists` only passes if no error is raised at all (its own `e.status` would raise AttributeError); the other three create the same bucket twice through boto3's resource API. LocalStack passes `recreate_not_overriding` and `create_exists`. The same call breaks the S3 Select test `test_json_column_sum_min_max`, which creates its bucket twice.

groups.title: ListObjects echoes an empty `Delimiter`
groups.why: `assert not 'Delimiter' in response` fails: with `delimiter=` (empty) the response carries `<Delimiter></Delimiter>`; AWS omits it. MinIO and LocalStack pass.

groups.title: ListObjects with delimiter + prefix + max-keys reports the wrong IsTruncated / paging
groups.why: `assert response['IsTruncated'] == is_truncated` (`assert True == False`) in the paged walk over keys with `_` / common prefixes. The v2 variants pass on MinIO and LocalStack.

groups.title: `encoding-type=url` encodes a space as `+` instead of `%20`
groups.why: Common prefix `quux ab/` comes back as `quux+ab/`; boto3 only decodes `%XX`, so the test (and LocalStack, which passes) expect `quux%20ab/`.

groups.title: ListObjects `Prefix` echo of a control character is URL-encoded in the wrong place
groups.why: Prefix `\n` comes back as `%0A` after boto3 decoding (`assert '%0A' == '\n'`), i.e. the value is encoded although the request did not ask for `encoding-type=url`, or encoded twice. Fails on MinIO and LocalStack too, so the exact AWS behaviour is unconfirmed.

groups.title: ListObjects v1 omits `<Marker/>` and `<Owner>`; v2 FetchOwner ignored
groups.why: `KeyError: 'Marker'` (empty marker must be echoed), `KeyError: 'Owner'` (v1 returns Owner per key by default) and `assert 'Owner' in objs_list[0]` with `fetch-owner=true`. MinIO and LocalStack pass the `Marker` and `fetchowner` cases.

groups.title: DeleteObjects accepts more than 1000 keys
groups.why: AWS answers 400 `MalformedXML`; fakes3 deletes all 1001 (`ClientError not raised`). MinIO passes.

groups.title: Content-MD5 validation: empty value accepted, malformed value reported as BadDigest
groups.why: Empty `Content-MD5:` is accepted (AWS: 400 `InvalidDigest`); a value that is not 16 base64-decoded bytes gives `BadDigest` (AWS: `InvalidDigest`). `BadDigest` is for a well-formed digest that does not match the body.

groups.title: GetBucketPolicyStatus returns NoSuchBucketPolicy for buckets without a policy
groups.why: The five `*_bucket_policy_status` tests compute `IsPublic` from ACL / policy; fakes3 returns 404 `NoSuchBucketPolicy` whenever no policy document exists, so public-ACL buckets cannot be reported. MinIO passes two of the five.

groups.title: Lifecycle: rule without ID is returned without one; invalid transition `Date` accepted
groups.why: AWS generates a rule ID when none is given (`assert 'ID' in lc_rule`) and rejects `Transitions[].Date` that is not ISO 8601 midnight (`20220927`) with 400 `MalformedXML`/`InvalidArgument`. MinIO passes the first, MinIO and LocalStack the second.

groups.title: Bucket policy: `Effect: Allow` with `NotPrincipal` is accepted
groups.why: AWS rejects it with 400 `MalformedPolicy` (NotPrincipal is only valid with Deny). MinIO passes.

groups.title: Object Lock: GOVERNANCE→COMPLIANCE change without bypass allowed; invalid default retention reports InvalidArgument
groups.why: `put_object_retention` changing the mode of a GOVERNANCE-locked object without `x-amz-bypass-governance-retention` must be 403 `AccessDenied`; `Days`/`Years` <= 0 in a bucket default must be `InvalidRetentionPeriod`, fakes3 says `InvalidArgument`.

groups.title: SSE request headers on GET/HEAD are ignored
groups.why: `x-amz-server-side-encryption(-aws-kms-key-id)` on GetObject/HeadObject must be 400 (AWS: only valid on writes). fakes3 serves the object (`ClientError not raised`). MinIO passes the GET case.

groups.title: SSE-C: UploadPart with a key that differs from CreateMultipartUpload returns 403, AWS returns 400
groups.why: `assert 403 == 400` in `test_encryption_sse_c_multipart_invalid_chunks_1` (MinIO and LocalStack pass) and in the three `test_copy_part_enc[…-sse-c-…]` cases that upload a part with the source's SSE-C key.

groups.title: GetObject `?partNumber=N` response lacks `x-amz-checksum-type`
groups.why: `KeyError: 'ChecksumType'` at `client.get_object(..., PartNumber=1)` for all five algorithms; HeadObject and GetObjectAttributes already report it.

groups.title: CompleteMultipartUpload accepts a malformed request-level checksum
groups.why: `ChecksumSHA256='bad'` on CompleteMultipartUpload must be 400 `BadDigest` (also when a part's checksum is omitted); fakes3 completes the upload.

groups.title: Responses carry an empty request id
groups.why: `ResponseMetadata.RequestId` is `''` and the error body has no `<RequestId>` element (`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'text'`). AWS (and MinIO, LocalStack) always send `x-amz-request-id` and `<RequestId>`, and clients log it.

groups.title: GetObject without a stored Content-Type omits the header
groups.why: `KeyError: 'ContentType'`: AWS answers `binary/octet-stream` for objects uploaded without one (MinIO passes).

groups.title: PutObject returns `x-amz-version-id` for unversioned / suspended buckets
groups.why: `assert not 'VersionId' in response`: the header must only appear when versioning is Enabled (fakes3 returns a VersionId). MinIO and LocalStack pass the single-part case.

groups.title: PutBucketVersioning with `MFADelete: Disabled` is rejected
groups.why: 403 `AccessDenied: Mfa Authentication must be used`. A `Disabled` value (what boto3 sends when asked to keep MFA off) must not require the `x-amz-mfa` header; only changing MFADelete to Enabled / toggling it does. MinIO and LocalStack pass.

groups.title: PutObjectTagging with 11 tags returns 500
groups.why: `assert 500 == 400`: must be 400 `InvalidTag`; a 500 means an unhandled error path.

groups.title: `x-amz-tagging` tags are returned in header order, AWS returns them sorted by key
groups.why: `foo=bar&bar` → fakes3 `[foo, bar]`, expected `[bar, foo]`. MinIO passes.

groups.title: CORS: wildcard origins (`*.suffix`) do not match
groups.why: `access-control-allow-origin` missing for `Origin: foo.suffix` against a rule with `AllowedOrigins: ['*.suffix']`. AWS allows a single `*` anywhere in the origin.

groups.title: POST policy uploads: invalid expiration format accepted, redirect Location not URL-encoded, `tagging` form field ignored, checksum fields rejected
groups.why: `test_post_object_invalid_date_format` gets 204 instead of 400; `success_action_redirect` Location ends in `etag="…"` while AWS encodes the quotes as `%22`; the `tagging` form field is not applied (`assert [] == [{'Key': '0', …}]`); `x-amz-checksum-*` form fields give 403 instead of 204.

groups.title: GET of a key that is not valid UTF-8 after percent-decoding returns 404
groups.why: `Key='\xae\x8a-'` must be 400 with message `Couldn't parse the specified URI.` (`fails_on_rgw`, i.e. AWS behaviour); fakes3 answers 404.

groups.title: Content-Encoding list re-serialised without the space (`deflate,gzip`)
groups.why: Stored as `deflate, gzip` with `aws-chunked`; fakes3 returns `deflate,gzip`. AWS returns the header the client sent minus `aws-chunked`. Unconfirmed against AWS; fails on MinIO and LocalStack too.

groups.title: HEAD of a deleted key in an unversioned bucket has no `x-amz-delete-marker: false`
groups.why: `KeyError: 'x-amz-delete-marker'` on the 404. The test expects the header; whether AWS sends it for unversioned buckets is unconfirmed (MinIO and LocalStack fail too).

groups.title: SigV2 PutObject with a truncated Content-Length answers 403 instead of 400 BadDigest
groups.why: `assert 403 == 400`; root cause not isolated (probably the same signature path as the SigV2 group, but PutObject paths sign correctly, so it may be a fakes3 body-length check).

groups.title: PutBucketLogging / bucket logging (NotImplemented)
groups.why: `PutBucketLogging is not implemented yet` (501). 5 AWS-applicable tests here; a further 31+ `bucket_logging` tests are marked `fails_on_aws` (they test RGW's journal/flush extension) and fail the same way.

groups.title: `x-amz-expected-bucket-owner` is not enforced
groups.why: A wrong ExpectedBucketOwner must be 403 `AccessDenied`; fakes3 ignores the header (`ClientError not raised`).

groups.title: ListBuckets `MaxBuckets` / `ContinuationToken`
groups.why: `list_buckets(MaxBuckets=1)` returns every bucket in the account (`assert 5 == 0` on the first call). The test also assumes an empty account, but the naming tests leave buckets such as `foo-.bar` behind (their names do not carry the test prefix, so the suite's cleanup skips them); it fails the same way in a serial run.

groups.title: GetObjectTorrent (`?torrent`)
groups.why: `assert 501 == 404`: fakes3 answers NotImplemented; AWS answers 404 NoSuchKey for a missing key and has deprecated the API for new buckets.

groups.title: SigV2: bucket-level requests signed by botocore fail with SignatureDoesNotMatch
groups.why: botocore signs the CanonicalizedResource of a path-style bucket request as `/bucket/` (trailing slash) although the request line is `/bucket`; verified with a stub server and boto3 1.43.123 (`CreateBucket`, `ListObjects`, `HeadBucket` sign `/bkt/`, `PutObject` signs `/bkt/k`). s3s builds the StringToSign from `req_uri.path()` verbatim (`s3s-sigv2` `create_string_to_sign`, called from `ops/signature.rs` `v2_check_header_auth`), so the signatures differ. Every SigV2 bucket-level call from boto3 is affected, not only these tests.

groups.title: SigV2: bad `x-amz-date` / `Date` is 400 InvalidRequest, AWS says 403
groups.why: s3s `v2_check_header_auth` parses `x-amz-date` with the SigV4 ISO-8601 parser (`invalid x-amz-date`) and `Date` as HTTP-date (`invalid date`, `missing date`), all mapped to 400 `InvalidRequest`; AWS answers 403 `AccessDenied` / `RequestTimeTooSkewed` and accepts RFC 1123 in `x-amz-date` for SigV2.

groups.title: SigV4: RFC 1123 `X-Amz-Date` together with `Date` is reported as `missing header: x-amz-date`
groups.why: `extract_amz_date` in s3s `ops/signature.rs:750` raises `InvalidRequest: missing header: x-amz-date` when the header is not in the compact ISO-8601 form; LocalStack accepts the request.

groups.title: PutObject with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (no Content-Length) is rejected
groups.why: `MissingContentLength: missing header: content-length`, raised in s3s `ops/signature.rs` (lines 709/875) before fakes3 sees the request. LocalStack accepts it.

groups.title: POST policy violations are 400 InvalidPolicyDocument, AWS says 403 AccessDenied
groups.why: Condition checks live in s3s `post_policy.rs` (`InvalidPolicyDocument`); AWS answers 403 `AccessDenied: Invalid according to Policy`. MinIO passes all four.

groups.title: Test mutates a header that boto3 re-signs afterwards (the request is valid)
groups.why: The tests add/remove `Authorization`, `Content-Length` or `x-amz-date` in a `before-call` hook, but botocore's signer rewrites those after the hook (checked with boto3 1.43.123 against a stub server: `Authorization` is replaced, `Content-Length` restored, `Date` re-added). The server correctly accepts the valid request, so `ClientError not raised`. They also fail on MinIO and LocalStack. Most are `fails_on_rgw` with a TODO saying so.

groups.title: `check_grants` sorts grants by a key that is None for group grantees (Python 3 TypeError)
groups.why: `got.sort(key=lambda x: x['Grantee'].get('DisplayName'))` runs whenever the first grant has a DisplayName; a group grant (AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers) has none, so Python 3 raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str'`. fakes3 lists the owner first, like AWS; MinIO and LocalStack fail identically.

groups.title: SSE-KMS tests expect the key id echoed verbatim; AWS (and fakes3) return the key ARN
groups.why: `assert 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:000000000000:key/testkey-1' == 'testkey-1'` for `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`. AWS always returns the full key ARN; RGW echoes what was sent. The `test_copy_enc` / `test_copy_part_enc` cases with an SSE-KMS destination fail on the same comparison (`assert False` inside the `assert` lambda). Fails on MinIO and LocalStack too.

groups.title: GetObject `?partNumber` out of range: test expects 400 InvalidPart (RGW), AWS answers 416 InvalidPartNumber
groups.why: `assert 416 == 400` (and `'InvalidRequest' == 'InvalidPart'` for the SSE-C variant). fakes3 follows the S3 API reference (416). Fails on MinIO and LocalStack too.

groups.title: SSE-C read with the wrong key: test expects 400, AWS answers 403
groups.why: `assert 403 == 400` for GET with a well-formed but different customer key; S3 reports 403 `AccessDenied` for a key that does not match the stored MD5 (400 is for malformed/missing headers). Fails on MinIO too.

groups.title: GetBucketEncryption / DeleteBucketEncryption on a fresh bucket expect NotFound; AWS has had SSE-S3 default encryption on every bucket since January 2023
groups.why: `assert '' == 'ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError'`: fakes3 (like current AWS) reports the default AES256 configuration instead of an error. Fails on MinIO too.

groups.title: Re-creating an owned bucket expected to fail with BucketAlreadyExists (RGW)
groups.why: Same call as the CreateBucket group above but the test insists on 409 `BucketAlreadyExists`; on AWS us-east-1 this is a 200. The two groups cannot both pass.

groups.title: PutObject `If-None-Match: <etag>` expected to give 412 (RGW extension; AWS accepts only `*`)
groups.why: Each test passes the `*` cases and then sends `IfNoneMatch=<etag>` expecting 412. The S3 API reference documents only `If-None-Match: *` for PutObject / CompleteMultipartUpload. MinIO passes (it implements the extension); LocalStack fails.

groups.title: Second CompleteMultipartUpload on a finished upload expected to succeed (RGW `check_previously_completed`)
groups.why: `NoSuchUpload` on the repeated complete (the tests comment it as an 'extra' complete); `test_multipart_resend_first_finishes_last` lists PartNumber 1 twice in the complete request and gets `InvalidPart`. All fail on MinIO and LocalStack.

groups.title: Presigned URL with negative / over-long X-Amz-Expires: test expects 403, S3 answers 400
groups.why: `assert 400 == 403`. S3 rejects out-of-range `X-Amz-Expires` with 400 `AuthorizationQueryParametersError`; the test encodes RGW's 403.

groups.title: SSE-KMS without a key id expected to fail; AWS falls back to the managed `aws/s3` key
groups.why: `ClientError not raised` for `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` alone. MinIO and LocalStack reject it, AWS accepts it.

groups.title: Test expects a bucket policy with only an Allow to deny the owner
groups.why: Referer-conditioned `Allow` policy; the test then expects the bucket owner's own GET to be 403. An Allow can never remove the owner's access, so only RGW's policy engine behaves like that (`fails_on_rgw` TODO says it is being fixed).

groups.title: Non-ASCII user metadata expected to round-trip verbatim; AWS returns RFC 2047 `=?UTF-8?B?…?=`
groups.why: `'=?UTF-8?B?SGVsbG8gV29ybGTDqQ==?=' == 'Hello World\xe9'`. fakes3 deliberately encodes like AWS (via `s3s-rfc2047`); boto3 does not decode.

groups.title: Needs RGW's accelerated lifecycle clock (`rgw_lc_debug_interval`)
groups.why: The test waits `lc_debug_interval` seconds for 'one day' to pass; AWS and fakes3 count real days (fakes3 has a virtual clock, but s3-tests cannot drive it).

groups.title: Bucket policy used by the test has no `Resource` (invalid on AWS too)
groups.why: `MalformedPolicy: Syntax errors in policy` for a statement with only Principal/Action; AWS rejects it as well. The test relies on RGW.
